subject: MedLinc: data placement, cross-region failover & PII retention questions
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medlinc.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@medlinc.com>, security@medlinc.com
Date: 2026-06-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — data placement & retention clarifications

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for the demo today — good overview. A few items came up on our side we need clarified before we can move to procurement:

1) Region pinning: We need to confirm that production inference for our EU customers can be pinned to the eu-west-1 region and that cold backups can live in a different EU region only (no US copies). Is that supported?

2) Cross-region failover: In the event of a region outage, what's Redwood's recommended failover behaviour for pinned customers? We need details on RTO/RPO assumptions and whether data is replicated across regions automatically or only on opt-in.

3) PII & retention: We store PHI-adjacent metadata. Can you describe retention controls at the per-customer level (retention windows, deletion APIs) and whether request logs or full prompts/outputs are retained longer than customer-configured retention?

4) Logging & access: Who at Redwood can access raw request logs? We need an audit trail and the ability to scope log access to a small set of Redwod personnel.

I've attached our internal questionnaire to this thread to make it easier for your engineering team to answer. Can Ben or Karthik weight in on the feasibility and any known limitations?

Appreciate a short response with links to any docs/SOC artifacts you can share.

—Liam

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@medlinc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — data placement & retention clarifications

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear list and for sharing the questionnaire. High-level answers below; Ben/Karthik included for detailed technical notes. We'll attach our SOC2 summary and a short diagram for failover. If that looks good, we can schedule a 30-minute tech deep-dive this week.

1) Region pinning: Yes — Redwood supports per-customer region pinning. For EU customers you can pin to eu-west-1. Cold backups can be restricted to another EU-only region; by default Redwood does not copy backups to the US unless explicitly enabled by the customer or required for a specified DR arrangement.

2) Cross-region failover: For pinned accounts the standard behaviour is:
- Primary region handles all traffic.
- If primary region becomes unavailable, requests can be routed to a pre-configured warm standby in a secondary region. Standby must be enabled ahead of time (opt-in).
- Typical RTO for warm standby is 15–45 minutes depending on KV cache warm-up; RPO depends on replication window you select (near-zero for synchronous replication vs up to 1 hour for asynchronous replication). We will include a diagram.

3) PII & retention: Customers control retention windows at the project/account level via the Console API. Deletion requests are supported via API and our standard SLA for deletion is 72 hours for operational metadata and up to 7 days for cold backups (longer if held for legal reasons). By default, raw prompts/outputs are not retained past the configured retention window; we offer an option to redact or not persist PII at ingest.

4) Logging & access: Access to raw request logs is strictly role-based. We can restrict access to named Redwood engineers for troubleshooting; every access is logged and surfaced in audit logs that you can pull. For high-security customers we can integrate with your SIEM via syslog/forwarding and set up an access-control roster as part of the onboarding SOW.

Next steps: Ben/Karthik — can you provide the SOC2 summary, failover diagram, and a short note on the replication modes (sync vs async) plus any constraints for warm standby? Liam — are you available for a 30-minute tech session on Fri 10:00–10:30 PT?

Thanks,
Stephanie
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-07-01T09:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — data placement & retention clarifications

Hi Liam — Ben here (runtime infra). Quick technical clarifications and constraints so you have something to review before the deep-dive: 

- Backups & placement: Cold backups are snapshots stored in the cloud object store in the region(s) you choose. We support EU-only backup placement. If you choose warm standby with cross-region replication we use either continuous async replication (default for cost/latency) or synchronous replication (opt-in, higher cost) for critical state.

- RTO/RPO details:
  * Warm standby (async): RTO 15–45m, RPO up to 1 hour by default.
  * Warm standby (sync): RTO 10–20m, RPO near-zero.
  * Cold restore from snapshot: RTO measured in hours (depends on snapshot size).

- KV cache warming: Large context models will have longer KV warm-up; for strict latency SLAs we recommend pre-warmed standby or active-active with traffic steering. Active-active across regions is possible but requires legal/contractual review for cross-border data flows.

- PII redaction: We offer an ingest-layer redaction toggle and token-level masking. Redaction removes sensitive fields before they hit long-term storage; however, for debug traces we may retain short-lived diagnostic logs (48–72h) unless the redaction setting is applied to logs as well.

- Access controls & audits: All internal accesses generate an audit event with user, role, timestamp, and reason. For customers with strict requirements we can do per-request approvals or integrate with your IAM for just-in-time access.

I'll join the Fri session and bring a simple replication matrix. If you can share any particular dataflow constraints in the questionnaire (e.g., no cross-border replication even for ephemeral caches), we'll mark those as hard constraints in the SOW.

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
